1.e4 d5 2.d4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3 exf3 5..name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit Accepted: Gunderam Defence
1.e4 d5 2.d4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3 exf3 5..background: Gerhart Gunderam analysed it extensively and published his analysis in a book on the Blackmar-Diemer Gambit in 1984.

1.e4 d5 2.d4 dxe4 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.f3 exf3 5..strategy: Centralises the knight on a square from which it covers g4 and g6, two retreat squares of the bishop, and prepares to drive that bishop back with the g-pawn. White keeps the initiative the gambit pawn was paid for, and Black has to handle the bishop with care.

Guards the bishop with a pawn and opens the diagonal for the king's bishop, so that Black can develop and castle while keeping the extra pawn. The knight on e5 stays unchallenged, so Black must expect a kingside pawn advance against the bishop and a lasting initiative for the pawn.
